newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures narrowly mixed in early trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures narrowly mixed in early trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures were narrowly mixed in thin trade, as the May Day holidays in Europe, coupled with the elections in Britain, kept prices locked in tight ranges, traders and analysts said.

The small gains in June marks and Swiss francs were further eroded after U.S. economic data were released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT. June marks edged below $0.5811, as dollar/marks rose to 1.7270 spot marks.
"The numbers were dollar friendly," one currency trader. "But we are looking for a quiet day overall because many European banks are closed for May Day."

U.S. March personal income rose 0.6 percent, versus average trade estimates for up 0.4 percent. Spending was up 0.5 percent, as forecast. February's numbers were revised, with income up 0.8 percent, instead of up 0.9 percent, and spending up 0.5 percent, instead of up 0.3 percent.

U.S. weekly jobless claims showed some softening in the economy, as the number of claims rose to 347,000 for the week ended April 26. In the prior week, however, claims were revised to 319,000 from 324,000.
Traders, on average, had been looking for claims in the week ended April 26 to stand at 325,000.
However, several traders said June marks were likely to hold above the pivot point of $0.5804, as the dollar/mark was overbought.
"I think the dollar/mark has a better chance of trading back to 1.72 than 1.7385 spot," one currency broker said.
The dollar/mark's near-term range of 1.72 to 1.7385 currently corresponds to $0.5831 to $0.5770, which is near June mark's contract low of $0.5768.
However, June yen set a contract low of $0.007915 despite concerns about central bank intervention and talk of another knock-out option at 127.50 spot, traders said.

Support for June yen is at $0.007904, which is equivalent to the spot level of 127.30. Overnight, the spot rate rallied through that level, despite talk that $2 billion in knock-options rested at that level.
Further support is at $0.007892, or 127.50 spot yen.

June sterling was also marginally lower and traded inside Wednesday's ranges ahead of the results of the British elections. Exit polls are expected to be released soon after voting ends at 1600 CDT/2100 GMT.
Some traders also said sterling was quiet after heavy hedge fund selling bombarded the currency on Wednesday.
They said many funds believed that sterling was overvalued. Support is at 1.6190, the 50-day moving average, and at 1.6150.
Funds were reportedly good buyers of June Canadian dollars on Thursday morning, traders said.
"I think it has bottomed," he said, referring to June Canadian dollar's contract low of $0.7155 which was set on Tuesday.

At 0848 CDT/1348 GMT, June yen was off $0.000007 at $0.007918, marks were up $0.0011 at $0.5811, Swiss francs off $0.0005 at $0.6824, sterling was off $0.0002 at $1.6224, and Canadian dollars were up $0.0018 at $0.7197.
